leaders.nextRole: President Emeritus and Professor of Political Science
leaders.notes: Political scientist and Soviet/Russian studies scholar; 15th president, oversaw the university centennial and the rise of athletics to NCAA Division I. Anchor incumbent in office at the start of 1996.
16th president; joined TU in May 1996 after seven years leading Texas Tech, and led an eight-year period of major campus and academic growth. Died in 2024.

leaders.nextRole: Stepped aside for health reasons; recalled as president later in 2012
leaders.notes: 17th president; anthropologist who came from Claremont Graduate University. Briefly stepped aside in mid-2012 for health reasons before being recalled by the Board of Trustees.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the Lyle School of Engineering
leaders.notes: Served only from July to September 2012 before Steadman Upham was recalled to the presidency; his very short tenure was among the shortest in TU history.

leaders.nextRole: Stepped down due to illness; died July 2017
leaders.notes: Recalled by the Board of Trustees in October 2012 for a second term; stepped down in 2016 due to declining health and died the following year.

leaders.priorInstitution: University of Tulsa (internal; previously President of OU-Tulsa)

leaders.notes: 20th president; a psychiatrist who had joined TU in 2015 after eight years leading OU-Tulsa. His tenure spanned the contentious 'True Commitment' academic restructuring; he resigned in January 2020 after a medical episode.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice President (former Dean of the College of Law)
leaders.notes: Longtime TU law dean and provost who served as interim president from January 2020 until Brad Carson took office in July 2021.

leaders.priorTitle: Former U.S. Representative and Acting Under Secretary of Defense; professor
leaders.nextRole: Work on AI governance and global norms
leaders.notes: 21st president; former Oklahoma congressman and Pentagon official. Announced departure in May 2025 (effective May 31, 2025) to focus on AI governance.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President and Director of Athletics
leaders.notes: TU alumnus and former athletics director who served as interim president from mid-2025 until Stacy Leeds took office July 1, 2026.

leaders.priorTitle: Willard H. Pedrick Dean and Regents Professor of Law
leaders.priorInstitution: Arizona State University (Sandra Day O'Connor College of Law)
leaders.notes: 22nd president and first woman to lead TU; a 1997 TU law alumna and former Cherokee Nation Supreme Court justice. Took office July 1, 2026 after a national search.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Academic Affairs and Associate Professor of Religious Studies
leaders.notes: 31st president; Augustinian theologian who had joined Villanova's administration in 1987. Guided the university into the 21st century; died in 2015. Anchor incumbent in office in 1996.

leaders.priorTitle: Chair of the Department of Theatre
leaders.notes: 32nd president; Augustinian priest and theater scholar who chaired Villanova's Theatre Department from 1992. Elected December 2005 and assumed office September 8, 2006; still serving.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President for Non-Medical Affairs
leaders.notes: 12th president; philosopher whose 22-year tenure (tied for longest in WFU history) modernized the university. Died in 2008. Anchor incumbent in office in 1996.
13th president; historian of American religion and former Notre Dame provost (the first Protestant in that role). Assumed office July 1, 2005; served through June 30, 2021.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs (former interim Chancellor)
leaders.nextRole: Returning to faculty focused on science mentoring
leaders.notes: 14th president and first woman to lead Wake Forest; a cell biologist who had been Vanderbilt provost and interim chancellor. Took office July 1, 2021; announced in October 2025 she would step down.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the School of Business (Jones Graduate School of Business)
leaders.notes: 15th president; economist and former Rice Business dean named Poets & Quants Dean of the Year in 2025. Announced May 20, 2026; took office July 1, 2026.

leaders.notes: 3rd president and first native-born American to lead YU; credited with saving the institution financially. Served as chancellor 2003-2013; died in 2020. Anchor incumbent in office in 1996.

leaders.priorInstitution: Hillel: The Foundation for Jewish Campus Life
leaders.notes: 4th president and the first non-rabbi to lead YU; former Hillel international director and Cardozo Law associate dean. Inaugurated September 2003; stepped down in 2017.

leaders.priorTitle: Head of Hechal Shlomo (Center of Jewish Heritage), Jerusalem
leaders.priorInstitution: Hechal Shlomo, Jerusalem (formerly senior rabbi, The Jewish Center, Manhattan)
leaders.notes: 5th president; Modern Orthodox rabbi and scholar who had led Hechal Shlomo in Jerusalem and earlier served as senior rabbi of The Jewish Center. Began tenure June 5, 2017; still serving.
